record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Is every four-point subset of a circle Ramsey, meaning that for every number of colors r, all sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean spaces colored with r colors must contain a monochromatic congruent copy of that four-point circular set?

evidence.quote: Every 4-point subset of a circle is Ramsey.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ is called Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists $n = n(K,r)$ such that for every coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $r$ colors, there is a monochromatic subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is congruent (i.e., isometric via a Euclidean isometry of $\mathbb{R}^n$) to $K$.

Prove or disprove: every 4-point subset of a circle in the plane is Ramsey. Equivalently, for every set $K = \{p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4\}$ of four points lying on a common circle, and for every positive integer $r$, there exists $n$ such that any $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $K$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every 4-point subset of a circle is Ramsey remains open in general. Křiž proved it in the special case where the four points form a trapezoid (a pair of opposite sides parallel). General 4-point cyclic sets are typically not subtransitive, and existing techniques (transitive/solvable symmetry groups, non-sphericality) do not apply, leaving the full conjecture unresolved as of recent surveys and REU/expository papers.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: every 4-point subset of a circle is Ramsey; known for trapezoids via Křiž.
status_evidence.claim: The 4-point-on-a-circle conjecture is listed as an open conjecture, with the trapezoid case settled.

status_evidence.title: The Biggest Open Problem in Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Patel, REU 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Almost all 4-point subsets of the circle are not subtransitive, so existing tools do not apply.
status_evidence.claim: The full conjecture remains open; only special cases like trapezoids are known.
